searchText: My only doubt about EIP-5133 is the motivation section: > Targeting for The Merge to occur mid-September 2022, trying to merge before block times noticeably slow down. To me this reads like a (semi-) official date for the Mainnet Merge. Is everybody okay with comitting to this? thats how I read it too That motivation was based on this section of the summary of the call yesterday: *"The first bit was about how much of a block time increase is acceptable, and whether we should aim for the delay to start kicking in when we expect to be ready to merge, or for blocks to not be exceeding X time. After some back and forth, we’ve converged on the former: trying to Merge before block times noticeably slow down."* Agree, I am not ready to commit to this. Imo the EIP should only specify the bomb delay, discussions/opinions about the merge must not be part of this EIP Seems like at some point the "before" got removed. Would everyone be comfortable with: "Targeting for The Merge to occur before mid-September 2022" (similar to EIP-4345 *"Targeting for The Merge to occur before June 2022. If it is not ready by then, the bomb can be delayed further."*) There isn't really a "target" for the merge so much as there is some non-trivial probability that it happens "before mid-September 2022". That probability may be below 50%, all we can really say I think is that it is bigger than epsilon. Same as with Dec 2021 pushback: Targeting for the Shanghai upgrade and/or the Merge to occur before December 2021. Either the bomb can be readjusted at that time, or removed all together. I think it's better to deliver no promises rather than deliver false promises Can someone check my forkid calculations? Scheduling gray glacier at block `15050000` produces forkid `0xf0afd0e3` In our unit tests we scheduled the `MergeMainnetSplit` block at `15000000`, I rescheduled this fork to `18000000` in our tests, which produces forkid `0x4fb8a872` cc <@758579010027782144> <@524738020033691659> <@583892532644151312> Yes, I also get 0xf0afd0e3 We got the same one with our calculations We could opt for a straightforward motivation like > To avoid network degradation due to a premature activation of the difficulty bomb. Thoughts? As <@478178670637219840> discussed here ... > https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/985672797198106625 ... the chance of a chain split and the technical (and political) problems that could cause are relevant. And I don't think now is the time to get into those. If it makes sense technically (I can't really judge) I'd be in favor of simply removing the bomb at this point. Then it can't serve as that sort of signal. We can more carefully work things out once we really do have a date. 0xf0afd0e3 condirmed <@628018527470616606> do you mind approving the spec PR, too 🙂 ? Why do you have to prepare for split? If miners are strong enough, they can have fun with a non-bomb fork forever. Just enlist enough short-term Miners (the one also doing staking nodes) for smooth transition after merge

excerpts.author: gcolvin
excerpts.content:
As <@478178670637219840> discussed here ...
> https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/985672797198106625
... the chance of a chain split and the technical (and political) problems that could cause are relevant.  And I don't think now is the time to get into those.   If it makes sense technically (I can't really judge) I'd be in favor of simply removing the bomb at this point.  Then it can't serve as that sort of signal.  We can more carefully work things out once we really do have a date.
